title: replan_test's failure message names nothing: print the refusal
description:
replan_test.go:79 fails with 'closed [], want every tick of the epic' and nothing else. When it failed overnight in epic dha's gate, that message could not distinguish a load-caused timeout from a clock-skew refusal, and the investigation cost far more than the fix.

The run's own result carries the answer: adding result.Failure to that message would have named RefusedUnaddressed on the spot.

Cheap, and the same rule the refusals themselves follow — say the fact that explains the others (44q, rxe).
acceptance_criteria: The test's failure message names the run's refusal reason when there is one
closed_reason: Already satisfied by 2047f38a, landed in PR #16: replan_test.go:83 prints the run's state and refusal instead of a bare 'closed []'.
